prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: syngonium went all droopy

so he was fine a few days ago - sitting upright and he gets a few hours from the humidifier everyday (although for 3 days it's been broken but fixed now and back on schedule). i checked the bottom and he's growing out a bit but i only repotted him at the beginning of october and it's winter now so i don't really want to mess with him too much. i thought maybe lack of humidity was the problem but any other suggestions are greatly appreciated 😁😁

it was a freebie from someone so i really had no clue what to do with it ! i suspect i've underwatered then - the room is very hot (and i think the pot is about 2.5-3" so yeah probably dries out too quick) :)

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
This looks most likely like **thirst from a hot, dry room**, with the humidifier outage making it worse. Syngonium droop when the soil dries out, and they usually perk up within hours of a good watering. The roots in your bottom photo are white and firm, with no sign of rot, which is encouraging.

The cat planter is the catch. Ceramic pots without drainage holes can trap water at the bottom, so the nursery pot may be sitting in a puddle even when the top looks dry. Check before you water again:

1. **Check the soil.** Push a finger 2-3 cm (about an inch) into the soil. If it feels dry, water. If it's still damp, don't water yet, even if the leaves droop.
2. **Check the bottom.** Lift the nursery pot out of the cat. If there's standing water in the cat, tip it out. If the nursery pot is sitting in water, that's a bigger problem than thirst.
3. **Water properly.** Take the plant out of the cat and water it thoroughly in the sink or over a basin until water runs out the holes. Let it drain fully, then put it back in the cat. Water again only when the top few cm are dry, probably every few days in your heat.

Don't repot now. You're right that it's a bad time for it, and the roots look healthy.

To keep it from wilting again, get the humidifier running consistently, or group it with other plants to raise humidity. Also keep it out of direct heat from radiators or vents, since that dries soil fast. Once it's watered and humid, the leaves should lift within a day or two. If they stay limp, or the stems turn soft or dark at the base, the soil is probably staying too wet, and the fix changes to letting it dry out more.
